Shares of technology giant Apple (AAPL) had an interesting first calendar month of 2018. The stock dropped in February as guidance was short of expectations, helped by a huge pullback in the overall market. Concerns over iPhone sales built throughout the period, which may explain this piece I re Banc Of California Putting Its History Behind It
Banc of California (BANC) is a southern California regional bank with a market cap of $940 million and assets of just over $10 billion. The stock has been written about on SA and other places a number of times over the past few years, but now that the recent overhangs are moving into the rear-view mirror, I wanted to circle back and check on the company.
In the past, the bank has been incredibly fast growing with a steadily increasing stock price but the business has been clouded by scandals and negative headlines including an SEC investigation and allegations of loan fraud which, while embarrassing, don’t look like they will have a meaningful impact on the underlying company going forward. As a result, the company trades at a price to tangible book value of 1.3, which is roughly half the ratio peer U.S. banks with assets between $9.5bn and $13.0bn as of Feb. 2, 2018. As with most other banks, the common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 9.9% is reasonably strong, so there’s no concern there.
In February of this year, the company unveiled a set of strategic initiatives which would make the bank one of the best-run of its size.
Resolution of Overhangs
The main overhang on the bank is an SEC investigation, resulting in the resignation of Chairman and CEO Steven Sugarman. The allegations paint a messy picture of a growth-hungry bank with potential self-dealing and less-than-ideal board oversight. This was all capped off by a questionable decision to buy naming rights for a stadium partially owned by the former CEO’s brother. Around this time, a major holder, PL Capital, as well as other major shareholders took a more active role in the bank and pushed for changes and a more independent investigation of the allegations than the company was undertaking. The company announced they were being investigated by the SEC and the CEO and a board member resigned. In addition, there were other major changes to the Board of Directors which brought much stronger corporate governance to the organization.
Following the board of directors change, the company appointed an outsider CEO, Doug Bowers, to run the company. Following his appointment, Mr. Bowers purchased 57,000 shares on the open market at $17.56. As a result of these changes and numerous other high-level personnel changes since, including the General Counsel, Chief Human Resource Officer, Chief Credit Officer, and Managing Director, among others. The company is now essentially under entirely new management than the previous regime.
While there are still lawsuits being filed back and forth between parties, the company is starting to bring focus back to operating the business. During the April earnings call, management was asked about updates on the SEC investigation. They noted that they continue to cooperate, but indication of an all-clear signal has not been given. Independent investigations undertaken by the bank on the range of allegations has found no wrongdoing. Over the next year or two, these headlines should fade as it appears that no major acts of wrongdoing are found and the numerous leadership changes provide some comfort that there are no continuing illegal acts.
Strategic Initiatives
Now that the company has made progress on putting the past issues behind them, they are putting together a plan for the future. In February, the company initiatives are focused on three areas: core deposit growth, growth in lending, and reducing expenses by utilizing technology (CRM, etc.). By executing on these areas, the company intends to increase shareholder value.
In addition, they are selling off aspects of the business which the bank has chosen not to concentrate on including Banc Home Loans, a nationwide mortgage business. While this is a positive step, it will most likely obscure the core operations while the transactions take place. The key long-term targets for the company are noted below. The company has clarified that this is a three-year strategic plan. So, in this case, “long term” is around mid-2021.
As you would expect, following a roll-out of these initiatives in February, the company is executing as planned on them in the most recent quarterly update in April. These goals represent major increases in operational efficiency and profitability of the company. While reaching these goals in three years is a challenge, there is a significant amount of low-hanging fruit while cleaning up the balance sheet and operations from the frenetic growth of the past several years.
While it is a leap of faith to take the company management at their word on these initiatives, scrutiny and increased involvement from activists (including PL Capital, which holds a board seat) should keep management focused on the goals. In addition, a new compensation structure was rolled out that reinforces the focus on metrics investors pay attention to. Executive compensation is now based on core deposit growth, ROAA, loan growth and an adjusted efficiency ratio, in addition to minimum gaining thresholds around capital and credit quality.
As the company shows continued progress on meeting these targets over the next few years, management will start to regain credibility and trade at a price to tangible book value closer to peers.
Valuation
The regional bank ETF KBWR trades at an average P/E ratio of 16.7 and a P/B of 1.58. Banc of California currently trades at P/E ratio of 21.2 and a P/B of 1.27. The headline company valuation metrics seem reasonable based on the current overhangs and ROA. In fact, the headline ratios look somewhat expensive.
The underlying strength and potential profitability of the company is hidden behind the overhang of the investigations and lawsuits, as well as business lines and assets acquired in the process of the explosive growth the company experienced in previous years. In looking at the company’s forecast ratios, if the company grows assets at only 5% (less than the 15% or 20% growth rate that the company expects), by 2021 they will have around $12 billion in assets. Note I assumed lower growth rates because they need to do a fair bit of “shrinking to grow” to shift the business focus to improve profitability.
At a return on average assets of 1%, the three-year target for the company, they earn $120 million per year. Using a current industry-average P/E multiple of 17, the market cap of the company comes to $2 billion – more than twice the current market cap and a stock price in the upper $30s per share.
Given that I don’t have much confidence in my ability to pick the midsize bank average multiple three years from now, a more conservative multiple of 14 can be applied to the anticipated earnings. At that multiple, the market cap would be around $1.6 billion, implying a stock price in the low $30s. Along the way, investors can pick up a dividend just under 3%.
Technical Picture
The technical picture for the company isn’t particularly compelling either way at this point. It is trading around the middle of the stock price range over the past few years of roughly $17 to $23.
In addition, the company is trading around the middle of the price/book ratio range of the past few years.
For now, I’m not too focused on the headline P/E ratio of the company because, as mentioned above, it will be lumpy while operational changes are made. While this information doesn’t present a compelling signal, it does give you a good opportunity to gauge the market’s prospective on management credibility. The management team has laid out compelling and ambitious operational targets, and I’m tempted to give the new team the benefit of the doubt on their ability to execute on the targets – while watching the longer-term technicals to gauge the market’s prospective of the management team’s credibility.
Takeaway
Moving past the SEC investigation and ongoing lawsuits should allow the bank and new management team to shift focus back to the improving operating results from the company.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
